x: The runners, well bunched together, circled the field once and out through the village via the centre path, with Shields, Saunders, Carter and Jordan together in the lead, the Ealing “boys” well together a little behind them.
Carter and A.

After the usual rush at the start, Carter and Shields were making the pace with several Belgrave and T.V.H. men in close attendance. At Beverley Brook the field had become well strung out and Arthur Allum came through to take the lead and eventually to finish first, with Carter 2nd and Shields 3rd.

Flower was leading, closely followed by Carter, Rice, Taylor and Smith. Coming up the hill about 3 miles out, Carter had taken the lead and, running very strongly with that natural easy style of his, he was gradually dropping the rest of the field.

On the far side of the starting field Syd Warboys found a bit of speed and went through to the front, immediately causing Penny and Allum to draw away from the field. Going across the Golf links the order was Penny, Allum, Carter, J.
Carter's entrance as a bewhiskered policeman on a piebald steed, held up the action for some minutes, but eventually it concluded amid thunderous applause.
Penny was in the lead with Weatherill, the South London Harrier, and our hopes were soon raised when we saw Footer lying 6th, followed by Carter 8th, and Abberton 10th.

On leaving the starting field, the runners were bunched together, with Penny, Flower and Carter making the pace. At the Windmill, however, we had a surprise, for Penny had opened up a gap of 100 yards.
Penny, Allum, Footer, Flower, Carter and Taylor, upon their handsome win which has brought honour to the Club, and inspiration for those who follow.

Our representatives to score were: Footer 1, Penny 3, Carter 17, Flower 25, Allum 37, Mains 40. All of which brings us to this year's race, when our objective was achieved and our first win recorded; but before proceeding with the pleasant task of describing our success, I should like to make a few comments.

In a fast start Chantler was the best away, but was soon headed by Syd Warboys moving in his best style and taking the field along at a fast pace for about ¾ mile, when Tom Carter moved up to take the lead, followed closely by Allum, Shields, Rice and J.
In the Two Miles race we finished our six in the first six positions—a wonderful performance—with Carter beating Jordan in an inches finish in 9 min. 58 sec.

Our team in the 4 x 300 yards was the same as for the hundreds and we more or less thought we would finish in the same position as in that race. Kench went off first and handed over just behind Carter of Croydon.
Arthur Penny showed his best form to win from the scratch mark once again, and Carter and Shaw also displayed excellent running to fill the minor positions.
When the runners returned to the track for the finish, Carter had joined Allum and Saunders. Then Arthur remembered the hot water and flew down the straight to win from Saunders and Carter!

When the field was sighted, for the turn home, Carter was leading the pack, running comfortably, followed by Ring, Shields, Rice, and J. Flower, with our "South of the Thames" Juniors, Martin, Saunders and Chantler, close on their heels.
Cook was making the pace, and he was a few yards ahead with Penny, Allum, Carter and Footer lying next, and a crowd of others close up, while our old veteran, George Still, brought up in the rear.
The Senior Championship held from Coulsdon provided us with a fairly easy win, and we had the pleasure of supplying the first two home in Footer and Carter.
Footer, Ginty and Carter were especially prominent of ours. Returning from the first lap our good start had gone, but we were well placed with Surrey A.C. looking very dangerous.
We should have quite a number of men competing for various counties, Footer and Carter for Surrey, Allum, Shields Dan Patience and Taylor for Middlesex, and Parker for Sussex.
Carter leads Footer by a yard at the top of Copse Hill, and they stride up the steep incline like two horses, with no sign of fatigue. Then come Jack Flower, Shields, Allum, Ring D.

We can safely say that the fifth relay is the most critical one in the whole Brighton Relay and this year we entrusted it to Tom Carter, who soon had an old friend and opponent in Webster on his shoulder.
The 2 Miles was easily the most exciting race of the evening. Tom Carter, Jack Flower and Syd Ring were running for us and they had G.
We hope to fare well in the four remaining events and repeat our win of last year in the League. The men to represent us were: 3 miles, Ring (4); Carter (7); Allum (10); Ginty (11): and 440 yards, R.
Our scoring men were Ginty, Ring, Rice, Taylor, Allum, Parker; with Carter and D.
Carter, C.

The result of the race was never in doubt, barring accidents, as Arthur Penny took the lead from the start, and gradually drew away from the field, eventually winning as he pleased. At the half-distance he was 55 secs. in front of Carter, with Parker next, having a very bad time, and hereabouts he retired.

Champion, had been entrusted with the next stage of about 4½ miles to Handcross; but was unable to make any headway against his more experienced rival, and eventually handed over to Tom Carter with a deficit of 30 seconds.

Ten of our points were amassed in the one and two mile events through the events of Cohen, Carter, Shields and Taylor. Our remaining points came from Lee (440 yards), and Quackenbos and Grassau (High Jump).
We were also beaten in the Mile team race although our team was a make-shift one, and included Tom Carter, who had just previously competed in the Club 3 Miles championship.
Carter, E.

Penny was next, followed by Carter, Cohen, Ring, and Wood (who won the Surrey Junior Race the week after) in the first twenty places. Our hopes of repeating our win of last year were now very bright; and we next saw the field coming round Tattenham Corner led by Bert Footer, followed by Belton.
Unfortunately, we were denied the services of Arthur Penny and Alf Taylor, both of whom had leg troubles; and Carter was in the throes of a severe cold.
From the very start Pat Parker looked the winner and after the first mile he was leading, but followed very closely by Carter, Cohen, Stimpson and Ring, with the rest of the field in hot pursuit.
We then saw Les Cohen, Tom Carter, and Arthur Penny move away from the rest; although Dan Patience was running well close behind. In the last lap a hectic struggle ensued.
Dan Patience had come up to Pat Parker, and then came Les Cohen and Bert Footer followed by Tom Carter and then the Frenchmen, running more or less in a solid bunch.

A further invitation having been given by the Union Sportive Metropolitaine for us to compete in the above event was accepted and the following team was chosen to represent the Club: Carter, Cohen, Footer, Patience D., Parker, Penny, Tobin and Verney, accompanied by W.
Our teams have, in recent years, always seemed to give of their best in this race; and we hope that Tom Carter, in his first season as Captain, will have the honour of leading them to victory.
When they reached the far corner, Smart led Cohen by a yard with Carter and Verney just behind, followed by Arthur Penny, Harry Shields, Jerman, Herbert, Ring, Taylor, Frank Webb and Lucas.
Our Relay team (Bird, Blunden, Pritchard, Pack) win in fine style; and our lads in the Three Miles race (Smart, Cohen, Carter) gave us another team win.

But half a mile later across the golf links they had to "paddle" a small lake (to the amusement of the spectators, but not the runners) and here Arthur Penny, with a determined expression, moved away from the others with Tom Carter hard on his heels.

Close (S.A.C.) had an easy win and was followed home by two of our stalwarts, Carter and Jerman. The team race resulted in a dead heat between Mitcham A.C. and ourselves, both teams scoring 26 points.
It was decided to score 7 aside, and as Tom Carter and Wilf Rispin were turning out after illness, we were not too optimistic about the result.

Carter headed the field at the finish once again, but on this occasion second place in the team race was the best we could do. We missed the help of Bert Footer, ill, and of Shaw and Shields, who mistook the venue.
A four aside match between Shaftesbury H., British Workers S.A., Metropolitan Police A.C., and ourselves, over our course saw an inevitable Carter win, and an easy Belgraave team victory.

A Surrey County 7-Miles Race was held at Wimbledon—and seven of the first eight to finish were Belgravians. Carter showed the way round, and Belgrave scored another win. Middlesex County also tried a 7-Miles race on this day from Ruislip.
A good turn out and a good crowd—mainly to see Wooderson. A good race with Carter in his unbeatable mood; and a 30-points margin in our team win.
Need we tell you the name of the individual winner? Well it was, Carter.
Held at Chingford, and to our surprise both Carter and Belgrave were beaten. By two seconds and four points only respectively; but it just goes to show!

Tom Carter, without any "real" opposition, ran a training 3 miles and reeled off his laps in faultless style. Harry Shields had to fight for his second place in this event, and this alone made the race very entertaining to watch.

The 2 miles was a very steady affair for the first mile, when Tom Carter led with the Czech runner at his shoulder. The pace then warmed up, and the Czech runner fell behind the leading bunch, which consisted of Carter, Worboys, Attryde, Fox, and Bettiss.

Champion, ran clean away from his field, which included Les Cohen, Tom Carter and Frank Abberton. Right from the crack of the gun, Saunders went to the front and, lap by lap, increased his lead over the opposition.

Penny was next, followed by Carter, Cohen, Ring, and Wood (who won the Surrey Junior Race the week after) in the first twenty places. Our hopes of repeating our win of last year were now very bright; and we next saw the field coming round Tattenham Corner led by Bert Footer.
Third place in the club "10" behind Penny and Carter, was succeded by sixth place in the Southern when Belgrave could only manage third team position in a close fought race.

In 1932 young HARRY SHIELDS won the Middlesex Junior Cross-country Championship; and in 1933 the Club Championship at 7 miles had in its leading positions PENNY, ALLUM, CARTER; and a Belgrave v Cadogan match, in conjunction, gave Belgrave a 38 to 40 points win, six aside scoring.
